chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Any man who goes to a ruined well, extracts it, digs out its rivers (water channels), and develops it, then charity (khums/zakat) is upon him regarding it. And if it was land belonging to a man before him who was absent from it, neglected it, and let it become ruined, then he comes afterwards seeking it, then the earth is Allah's and for the one who develops it.'

key_terms.بَائِرَة: A specific type of ruined well or land

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on reviving abandoned or ruined land and wells?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of *iqha al-arad* (reviving dead lands), emphasizing that ownership is contingent upon active cultivation rather than mere title. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that neglect by an absent owner transfers the land to the reviver, linking this civil right to the spiritual obligation of paying charity (sadaqah) on the produce, thereby integrating economic activity with religious duty.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ahmad Bin Muhammad altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Whichever man goes to a ruined well so he extracts it and digs out its rivers and develops it, so there would be charity (to give) upon him with regards to it, and if it was a land of a man before him who was absent from it, and neglected it, so he had ruined it, then he comes afterwards, so the earth is Allah<sup>ajwj</sup>’s and for the one who develops it’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn Mahbub from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘

Whoever comes upon a ruined barren place, then finds out and digs its canals and builds it, he owes charity. If the land belonged to a man before him who has disappeared, abandoned it and ruined it, then came thereafter, he has to take notice that the land belongs to Allah and to those who build it.’”
